Reference Panel : Render ‣ Bake Bake Executes the bake operation using the current settings. Bake from Multires Bakes a Normal or Displacement map directly from a mesh that has a Multiresolution Modifier . This method compares two resolution levels of the modifier: Viewport Levels Used as the low-resolution base mesh. Render Levels Used as the high-resolution detailed mesh. The resulting bake represents the difference between these two levels, allowing detailed sculpted information to be captured as a texture map. Bake Type Determines what kind of surface information is extracted from the Multiresolution modifier. See Bake Types for more information. Normals : Bakes surface normal direction differences between the two levels. Displacement : Bakes height differences as a grayscale displacement map. Vector Displacement : Bakes full 3D positional offsets as a vector displacement map. Bake Type Type of pass to bake. Combined : Bakes all materials, textures, and lighting except specularity. The passes that contribute to the combined pass can be toggled individually to form the final map. Ambient Occlusion : Bakes ambient occlusion as specified in the World panels. Ignores all lights in the scene. Shadow : Bakes shadows and lighting. Normal : Bakes normals to an RGB image. UV : Mapped UV coordinates, used to represent where on a mesh a texture gets mapped too. This is represented through the red and green channels of the image, the blue channel is encoded with a constant value of 1 but does not hold any information. Roughness : Bakes the roughness pass of a material. Emit : Bakes Emission, or the Glow color of a material. Reference Panel : Physics ‣ Fluid ‣ Settings Type : Flow Flow Type Smoke : Emit only smoke. Fire + Smoke : Emit both fire and smoke. Fire : Emit only fire. Note that the domain will automatically create some smoke to simulate smoke left by burnt fuel. Liquid : Emit liquid. Flow Behavior Controls if the Flow object either adds ( Inflow ), removes ( Outflow ), or turns the mesh itself into fluid ( Geometry ). Inflow : This object will emit fluid into the simulation, like a water tap or base of a fire. Outflow : Any fluid that enters the Bounding Box of this object will be removed from the domain (think of a drain or a black hole). This can be useful in combination with an inflow to prevent the whole domain from filling up. Outflow objects can be animated and the area where the fluid disappears will follow the object as it moves around. Geometry : All regions of this object that are inside the domain bounding box will be used as actual fluid in the simulation. You can place more than one fluid object inside the domain. Also make sure that the surface normals are pointing outwards or else they will not simulate properly. In contrast to domain objects, the actual mesh geometry is used for fluid objects. Use Flow Inflow Outflow Enables or disables the flow of fluid, this property is useful for animations to selectively enable and disable when fluid is being added to or removed from the domain. Sampling Substeps Number of sub-steps used to reduce gaps in emission of fluid from fast-moving sources. Comparison of smoke inflow quickly rising upwards at different sub-step rates. Registering a class with Blender results in the class definition being loaded into Blender, where it becomes available alongside existing functionality. Once this class is loaded you can access it from bpy.types , using the bl_idname rather than the classes original name. Note There are some exceptions to this for class names which aren’t guarantee to be unique. In this case use: bpy.types.Struct.bl_rna_get_subclass_py() . When loading a class, Blender performs sanity checks making sure all required properties and functions are found, that properties have the correct type, and that functions have the right number of arguments. Mostly you will not need concern yourself with this but if there is a problem with the class definition it will be raised on registering: Using the function arguments def execute(self, context, spam) , will raise an exception: ValueError: expected Operator, SimpleOperator class "execute" function to have 2 args, found 3 Using bl_idname = 1 will raise: TypeError: validating class error: Operator.bl_idname expected a string type, not int Inter-Class Dependencies When customizing Blender you may want to group your own settings together, after all, they will likely have to co-exist with other scripts. Provides Python access to calling operators, this includes operators written in C++, Python or macros. Only keyword arguments can be used to pass operator properties. Operators don’t have return values as you might expect, instead they return a set() which is made up of: {'RUNNING_MODAL', 'CANCELLED', 'FINISHED', 'PASS_THROUGH'} . Common return values are {'FINISHED'} and {'CANCELLED'} , the latter meaning that the operator execution was aborted without making any changes or saving an undo history entry. If operator was cancelled but there wasn’t any reports from it with {'ERROR'} type, it will just return {'CANCELLED'} without raising any exceptions. However, if there are error reports, a RuntimeError will be raised after the operator finishes execution, including all error report messages, regardless of the return status (even if it was {'FINISHED'} ). Calling an operator in the wrong context will raise a RuntimeError , there is a poll() method to avoid this problem. Note that the operator ID (bl_idname) in this example is mesh.subdivide , bpy.ops is just the access path for Python. Keywords and Positional Arguments For calling operators keywords are used for operator properties and positional arguments are used to define how the operator is called. There are 2 optional positional arguments (documented in detail below). bpy . ops . test . operator ( execution_context , undo ) execution_context - str (enum). undo - bool type. Blender has an embedded Python interpreter which is loaded when Blender is started and stays active while Blender is running. This interpreter runs scripts to draw the user interface and is used for some of Blender’s internal tools as well. Blender’s embedded interpreter provides a typical Python environment, so code from tutorials on how to write Python scripts can also be run with Blender’s interpreter. Blender provides its Python modules, such as bpy and mathutils , to the embedded interpreter so they can be imported into a script and give access to Blender’s data, classes, and functions. Scripts that deal with Blender data will need to import the modules to work. Here is a simple example which moves a vertex attached to an object named “Cube”: import bpy bpy . data . objects [ "Cube" ] . data . vertices [ 0 ] . co . x += 1.0 This modifies Blender’s internal data directly. When calling an operator you may want to pass the execution context. This determines the context that is given for the operator to run in, and whether invoke() is called or only execute(). EXEC_DEFAULT is used by default, running only the execute() method, but you may want the operator to take user interaction with INVOKE_DEFAULT which will also call invoke() if existing. The execution context is one of: INVOKE_DEFAULT INVOKE_REGION_WIN INVOKE_REGION_CHANNELS INVOKE_REGION_PREVIEW INVOKE_AREA INVOKE_SCREEN EXEC_DEFAULT EXEC_REGION_WIN EXEC_REGION_CHANNELS EXEC_REGION_PREVIEW EXEC_AREA EXEC_SCREEN # Collection add popup. import bpy bpy . ops . object . collection_instance_add ( 'INVOKE_DEFAULT' ) It is also possible to run an operator in a particular part of the user interface. For this we need to pass the window, area and sometimes a region. # Maximize 3d view in all windows. import bpy from bpy import context for window in context . window_manager . windows : screen = window . screen for area in screen . areas : if area . type == 'VIEW_3D' : with context . temp_override ( window = window , area = area ): bpy . ops . screen . screen_full_area () break", "score": 0.4916489346227326, "source": "b2_blender_python_reference_5_0_bpy_ops_html_execution-context-_0.md", "doc_path": "blender_python_reference_5_0/bpy.ops.html#execution-context-", "doc_type": "manual"}], "code_snippets": ["python

---

Operators are tools generally accessed by the user from buttons, menu items or key shortcuts. From the user perspective they are a tool but Python can run these with its own settings through the bpy.ops module. Examples: >>> bpy . ops . mesh . flip_normals () {'FINISHED'} >>> bpy . ops . mesh . hide ( unselected = False ) {'FINISHED'} >>> bpy . ops . object . transform_apply () {'FINISHED'} Tip The Operator Cheat Sheet gives a list of all operators and their default values in Python syntax, along with the generated docs. This is a good way to get an overview of all Blender’s operators. Operator Poll() Many operators have a “poll” function which checks if the cursor is in a valid area or if the object is in the correct mode (Edit Mode, Weight Paint Mode, etc). Provides Python access to calling operators, this includes operators written in C++, Python or macros. Only keyword arguments can be used to pass operator properties. Operators don’t have return values as you might expect, instead they return a set() which is made up of: {'RUNNING_MODAL', 'CANCELLED', 'FINISHED', 'PASS_THROUGH'} . Common return values are {'FINISHED'} and {'CANCELLED'} , the latter meaning that the operator execution was aborted without making any changes or saving an undo history entry. If operator was cancelled but there wasn’t any reports from it with {'ERROR'} type, it will just return {'CANCELLED'} without raising any exceptions. However, if there are error reports, a RuntimeError will be raised after the operator finishes execution, including all error report messages, regardless of the return status (even if it was {'FINISHED'} ). Calling an operator in the wrong context will raise a RuntimeError , there is a poll() method to avoid this problem. Note that the operator ID (bl_idname) in this example is mesh.subdivide , bpy.ops is just the access path for Python. Keywords and Positional Arguments For calling operators keywords are used for operator properties and positional arguments are used to define how the operator is called. When calling an operator you may want to pass the execution context. This determines the context that is given for the operator to run in, and whether invoke() is called or only execute(). EXEC_DEFAULT is used by default, running only the execute() method, but you may want the operator to take user interaction with INVOKE_DEFAULT which will also call invoke() if existing. The execution context is one of: INVOKE_DEFAULT INVOKE_REGION_WIN INVOKE_REGION_CHANNELS INVOKE_REGION_PREVIEW INVOKE_AREA INVOKE_SCREEN EXEC_DEFAULT EXEC_REGION_WIN EXEC_REGION_CHANNELS EXEC_REGION_PREVIEW EXEC_AREA EXEC_SCREEN # Collection add popup. import bpy bpy . ops . object . collection_instance_add ( 'INVOKE_DEFAULT' ) It is also possible to run an operator in a particular part of the user interface. Blender’s text editor is fine for small changes and writing tests but its not full featured, for larger projects you’ll probably want to use a standalone editor or Python IDE. Editing a text file externally and having the same text open in Blender does work but isn’t that optimal so here are two ways you can use an external file from Blender. Using the following examples you’ll still need text data-block in Blender to execute, but reference an external file rather than including it directly. Executing External Scripts This is the equivalent to running the script directly, referencing a script’s path from a two line code block. filename = "/full/path/to/myscript.py" exec ( compile ( open ( filename ) . read (), filename , 'exec' )) You might want to reference a script relative to the blend-file. import bpy import os filename = os . path . join ( os . path . dirname ( bpy . data . filepath ), "myscript.py" ) exec ( compile ( open ( filename ) . read (), filename , 'exec' )) Executing Modules This example shows loading a script in as a module and executing a module function. import myscript import importlib importlib . reload ( myscript ) myscript . main () Notice that the script is reloaded every time, this forces use of the modified version, otherwise the cached one in sys.modules would be used until Blender was restarted. The important difference between this and executing the script directly is it has to call a function in the module, in this case main() but it can be any function, an advantage with this is you can pass arguments to the function from this small script which is often useful for testing different settings quickly. Common return values are {'FINISHED'} and {'CANCELLED'} , the latter meaning that the operator execution was aborted without making any changes or saving an undo history entry. If operator was cancelled but there wasn’t any reports from it with {'ERROR'} type, it will just return {'CANCELLED'} without raising any exceptions. However, if there are error reports, a RuntimeError will be raised after the operator finishes execution, including all error report messages, regardless of the return status (even if it was {'FINISHED'} ). Calling an operator in the wrong context will raise a RuntimeError , there is a poll() method to avoid this problem. Note that the operator ID (bl_idname) in this example is mesh.subdivide , bpy.ops is just the access path for Python. Keywords and Positional Arguments For calling operators keywords are used for operator properties and positional arguments are used to define how the operator is called. {"code":"import bpy
import os
import math
from mathutils import Vector
import bmesh

# =============================================================
# Oil Pour (Mantaflow Liquid) - Blender 5.0
# Asset: oil_pour_20260202_021508
# Notes:
# - Fluid dset.* and fset.* assignments are restricted to VERIFIED API list.
# - Some requested artistic/physical controls (viscosity_base/exponent, use_plane_init,
#   adaptive domain bounds, caustics toggles) are NOT in the verified spec, therefore
#   are not set here. Blender defaults will be used.
# =============================================================

ASSET_NAME = "oil_pour_20260202_021508"
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 48
FPS = 24

# Output locations
OUTPUT_DIR = os.path.join("/tmp", "blender_vfx", ASSET_NAME)
FRAME_DIR = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "frames")
CACHE_DIR = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "mantaflow_cache")

for p in (OUTPUT_DIR, FRAME_DIR, CACHE_DIR):
    os.makedirs(p, exist_ok=True)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Utilities
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def deselect_all():
    for o in bpy.context.view_layer.objects:
        o.select_set(False)


def set_active(obj):
    deselect_all()
    obj.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj


def look_at(obj, target, track='-Z', up='Y'):
    """Orient obj to look at target."""
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    quat = direction.to_track_quat(track, up)
    obj.rotation_euler = quat.to_euler()


def clear_scene():
    # Ensure object mode
    if bpy.ops.object.mode_set.poll():
        try:
            bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='OBJECT')
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Delete all objects
    deselect_all()
    for obj in list(bpy.data.objects):
        obj.select_set(True)
    if bpy.ops.object.delete.poll():
        bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Remove orphan data blocks (conservative)
    for datablock in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.cameras):
        for block in list(datablock):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablock.remove(block)


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Scene setup
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def setup_scene():
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    scene.frame_start = FRAME_START
    scene.frame_end = FRAME_END
    scene.render.fps = FPS

    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = 256
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'

    scene.render.resolution_x = 1920
    scene.render.resolution_y = 1080
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100

    scene.render.image_settings.file_format = 'PNG'
    scene.render.image_settings.color_mode = 'RGBA'
    scene.render.film_transparent = False

    # Color management: warm product-shot contrast
    try:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'
        scene.view_settings.exposure = 0.2
    except Exception:
        pass


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Materials
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def make_material_oil():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Oil")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links

    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
    out.location = (520, 0)

    principled = nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled")
    principled.location = (200, 0)

    # Oil base: amber-gold with slight green hint
    principled.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (0.85, 0.65, 0.15, 1.0)
    principled.inputs["Transmission Weight"].default_value = 1.0
    principled.inputs["IOR"].default_value = 1.47
    principled.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.035
    principled.inputs["Subsurface Weight"].default_value = 0.03
    principled.inputs["Subsurface Color"].default_value = (0.85, 0.65, 0.15, 1.0)

    # Volume absorption for rich color depth
    vol_abs = nodes.new("ShaderNodeVolumeAbsorption")
    vol_abs.location = (200, -220)
    vol_abs.inputs["Color"].default_value = (0.95, 0.70, 0.20, 1.0)
    vol_abs.inputs["Density"].default_value = 2.5

    # Subtle micro-variation in roughness
    noise = nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
    noise.location = (-220, -40)
    noise.inputs["Scale"].default_value = 25.0
    noise.inputs["Detail"].default_value = 2.0
    noise.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.5

    mapr = nodes.new("ShaderNodeMapRange")
    mapr.location = (-10, -40)
    mapr.inputs["From Min"].default_value = 0.3
    mapr.inputs["From Max"].default_value = 0.7
    mapr.inputs["To Min"].default_value = 0.02
    mapr.inputs["To Max"].default_value = 0.06

    links.new(noise.outputs["Fac"], mapr.inputs["Value"])
    links.new(mapr.outputs["Result"], principled.inputs["Roughness"])

    links.new(principled.outputs["BSDF"], out.inputs["Surface"])
    links.new(vol_abs.outputs["Volume"], out.inputs["Volume"])

    return mat


def make_material_glass():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Glass")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links

    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
    out.location = (420, 0)

    principled = nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled")
    principled.location = (120, 0)

    principled.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    principled.inputs["Transmission Weight"].default_value = 1.0
    principled.inputs["IOR"].default_value = 1.52
    principled.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.0

    links.new(principled.outputs["BSDF"], out.inputs["Surface"])

    return mat


def make_material_table():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Table")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes

    principled = nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if principled:
        principled.inputs["Base Color"].default_value = (0.95, 0.93, 0.90, 1.0)
        principled.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.45
    return mat


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Geometry creation
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def create_table_and_backdrop(table_mat):
    # Table plane
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=2.0, location=(0, 0, 0))
    table = bpy.context.active_object
    table.name = "Table"
    table.data.materials.append(table_mat)

    # Backdrop plane (simple cyclorama-ish)
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=2.0, location=(0, 0.7, 1.0))
    back = bpy.context.active_object
    back.name = "Backdrop"
    back.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0, 0)
    back.data.materials.append(table_mat)

    # Slight bevel/smoothing for nicer light falloff
    if bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth.poll():
        set_active(back)
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    return table, back


def create_glass(glass_mat):
    # Outer cylinder
    radius = 0.04  # 8cm diameter
    height = 0.12  # 12cm tall

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=128, radius=radius, depth=height, location=(0, 0, height * 0.5))
    glass = bpy.context.active_object
    glass.name = "Glass"

    # Remove top face to make it open
    me = glass.data
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)

    top_z = max(v.co.z for v in bm.verts)
    faces_top = [f for f in bm.faces if all(v.co.z > top_z - 1e-6 for v in f.verts)]
    if faces_top:
        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=faces_top, context='FACES')

    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()

    # Solidify to create wall thickness
    solid = glass.modifiers.new(name="Solidify", type='SOLIDIFY')
    solid.thickness = -0.003  # inward, ~3mm wall
    solid.offset = 1.0

    # Bevel for rim highlight
    bev = glass.modifiers.new(name="Bevel", type='BEVEL')
    bev.width = 0.001
    bev.segments = 3

    # Shade smooth
    set_active(glass)
    if bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth.poll():
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    # Material
    glass.data.materials.append(glass_mat)

    return glass


def create_domain_cube():
    # Domain should comfortably contain glass and pour height.
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=(0, 0, 0.25))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "FluidDomain"

    # 0.30 x 0.30 x 0.50 meters
    domain.scale = (0.15, 0.15, 0.25)

    # Hide domain object itself in render (mesh output will be rendered via modifier)
    domain.display_type = 'WIRE'

    return domain


def create_flow_inflow_emitter():
    # Create a small disc that represents the stream cross-section.
    # Kept planar to aim velocity along its normal.
    z = 0.12 + 0.15  # glass rim + 15cm
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_circle_add(vertices=64, radius=0.004, fill_type='NGON', location=(0, 0, z))
    emitter = bpy.context.active_object
    emitter.name = "OilInflow"

    # Ensure the disc normal points +Z (default). We want downward initial velocity,
    # so we will use a negative velocity_normal.

    # Hide the emitter from render
    emitter.hide_render = True
    emitter.display_type = 'WIRE'

    return emitter


def create_flow_initial_pool():
    # Initial amount of oil in the glass (geometry flow)
    # Approximate ~150ml with h ~ 0.03-0.04m.
    radius_inner = 0.037
    height = 0.035
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=96, radius=radius_inner, depth=height, location=(0, 0, height * 0.5 + 0.002))
    pool = bpy.context.active_object
    pool.name = "OilInitialPool"
    pool.hide_render = True
    pool.display_type = 'WIRE'

    return pool


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Lighting and Camera
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def create_lighting():
    # Warm backlight (key)
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(0.0, 0.35, 0.25))
    key = bpy.context.active_object
    key.name = "Light_Key_Back"
    key.data.energy = 1200
    key.data.size = 0.35
    key.data.color = (1.0, 0.86, 0.55)  # warm golden
    look_at(key, Vector((0, 0, 0.08)), track='-Z', up='Y')

    # Soft fill front-left
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(-0.22, -0.25, 0.18))
    fill = bpy.context.active_object
    fill.name = "Light_Fill"
    fill.data.energy = 350
    fill.data.size = 0.45
    fill.data.color = (1.0, 0.95, 0.85)
    look_at(fill, Vector((0, 0, 0.08)), track='-Z', up='Y')

    # Rim / edge kicker
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(0.25, -0.10, 0.20))
    rim = bpy.context.active_object
    rim.name = "Light_Rim"
    rim.data.energy = 220
    rim.data.size = 0.25
    rim.data.color = (1.0, 0.90, 0.75)
    look_at(rim, Vector((0, 0, 0.08)), track='-Z', up='Y')

    return key, fill, rim


def create_camera(glass_obj):
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0.0, -0.42, 0.12))
    cam = bpy.context.active_object
    cam.name = "Camera"

    cam.data.lens = 85  # mm

    # DOF: focus on glass
    try:
        cam.data.dof.use_dof = True
        cam.data.dof.focus_object = glass_obj
        cam.data.dof.aperture_fstop = 2.4
    except Exception:
        pass

    look_at(cam, Vector((0, 0, 0.085)), track='-Z', up='Y')

    bpy.context.scene.camera = cam
    return cam


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Fluid setup (STRICT: only verified dset.* and fset.* attributes)
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def setup_domain(domain_obj, oil_mat):
    # Domain modifier
    mod = domain_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'DOMAIN'
    dset = mod.domain_settings  # MUST be named 'dset'

    # Verified attributes ONLY
    dset.domain_type = 'LIQUID'
    dset.resolution_max = 96
    dset.use_adaptive_timesteps = True
    dset.timesteps_max = 12

    dset.use_noise = False
    dset.noise_strength = 0.2
    dset.noise_scale = 2

    # Vorticity mainly affects gaseous sims; kept low.
    dset.vorticity = 0.05

    dset.cache_type = 'ALL'
    dset.cache_directory = CACHE_DIR

    # Verified enum includes ZIP; use ZIP (recommended for 5.0+).
    dset.openvdb_cache_compress_type = 'ZIP'

    dset.use_flip_particles = True
    dset.flip_ratio = 1.0
    dset.particle_radius = 1.0

    dset.use_mesh = True
    dset.mesh_smoothen_pos = 2
    dset.mesh_smoothen_neg = 2
    dset.mesh_concave_upper = 1.0

    dset.use_bubble_particles = True
    dset.use_foam_particles = False
    dset.use_spray_particles = False

    # Assign oil material to domain (mesh output will use it)
    if domain_obj.data.materials:
        domain_obj.data.materials[0] = oil_mat
    else:
        domain_obj.data.materials.append(oil_mat)

    return mod


def setup_flow_inflow(flow_obj):
    mod = flow_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # MUST be named 'fset'

    # Verified attributes ONLY
    fset.flow_type = 'LIQUID'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'INFLOW'

    # Downward initial velocity: disc normal is +Z, negative velocity emits down
    fset.use_initial_velocity = True
    fset.velocity_normal = -3.0

    fset.temperature = 0.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    return mod


def setup_flow_geometry(flow_obj):
    mod = flow_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # MUST be named 'fset'

    # Verified attributes ONLY
    fset.flow_type = 'LIQUID'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'GEOMETRY'

    fset.use_initial_velocity = False
    fset.velocity_normal = 0.0
    fset.temperature = 0.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    return mod


def setup_effector(glass_obj, table_obj):
    # Effector settings are left as Blender defaults.
    # IMPORTANT: Do not set unknown effector properties (not in verified spec).
    mod = glass_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'EFFECTOR'

    mod2 = table_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod2.fluid_type = 'EFFECTOR'


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Baking and Rendering
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def bake_simulation(domain_obj):
    print("\n--- Baking Mantaflow ---")
    print(f"Cache directory: {CACHE_DIR}")

    # Ensure domain is active for baking operators
    set_active(domain_obj)

    # Bake sequence: try full bake, else modular bakes.
    try:
        if bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all.poll():
            bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all()
            print("bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all finished")
            return
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"bake_all failed: {e}")

    # Fallback modular
    for op_name, op in (
        ("bake_data", bpy.ops.fluid.bake_data),
        ("bake_mesh", bpy.ops.fluid.bake_mesh),
        ("bake_particles", bpy.ops.fluid.bake_particles),
    ):
        try:
            if op.poll():
                op()
                print(f"bpy.ops.fluid.{op_name} finished")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"bpy.ops.fluid.{op_name} failed: {e}")


def render_frames():
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    print("\n--- Rendering frames ---")
    for fr in range(scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end + 1):
        scene.frame_set(fr)
        filepath = os.path.join(FRAME_DIR, f"{ASSET_NAME}_{fr:04d}.png")
        scene.render.filepath = filepath

        # Per-frame still render
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
        print(f"Rendered frame {fr} -> {filepath}")


def save_blend():
    blend_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f"{ASSET_NAME}.blend")
    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=blend_path)
    print(f"Saved .blend to: {blend_path}")


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    clear_scene()
    setup_scene()

    oil_mat = make_material_oil()
    glass_mat = make_material_glass()
    table_mat = make_material_table()

    table, back = create_table_and_backdrop(table_mat)
    glass = create_glass(glass_mat)

    # Fluids
    domain = create_domain_cube()
    inflow = create_flow_inflow_emitter()
    pool = create_flow_initial_pool()

{"code":"import bpy
import os
import math
from mathutils import Vector
import bmesh

# =============================================================
# Oil Pour (Mantaflow Liquid) - Blender 5.0
# Asset: oil_pour_20260202_021508

#
# CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
# - dset.* and fset.* assignments use ONLY VERIFIED API attributes.
# - Node socket names are NOT part of the fluid API spec; however this script
#   avoids hard failures by using safe socket setters.
#
# IMPORTANT LIMITATIONS (not in verified fluid API list, so not set):
# - viscosity_base / viscosity_exponent
# - flow use_plane_init
# - explicit adaptive domain bounds control
# - explicit surface tension controls
# =============================================================

ASSET_NAME = "oil_pour_20260202_021508"
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 48
FPS = 24

# Output locations
OUTPUT_DIR = os.path.join("/tmp", "blender_vfx", ASSET_NAME)
FRAME_DIR = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "frames")
CACHE_DIR = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "mantaflow_cache")

for p in (OUTPUT_DIR, FRAME_DIR, CACHE_DIR):
    os.makedirs(p, exist_ok=True)


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Utilities
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def deselect_all():
    for o in bpy.context.view_layer.objects:
        o.select_set(False)


def set_active(obj):
    deselect_all()
    obj.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj


def depsgraph_update():
    """Try to update depsgraph safely."""
    try:
        bpy.context.view_layer.depsgraph.update()
    except Exception:
        # Some builds expose update() directly on view_layer
        try:
            bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        except Exception:
            pass


def look_at(obj, target, track='-Z', up='Y'):
    """Orient obj to look at target."""
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    quat = direction.to_track_quat(track, up)
    obj.rotation_euler = quat.to_euler()


def safe_set_node_input(node, input_name, value):
    """Set node input by name if it exists (avoid KeyError across versions)."""
    sock = node.inputs.get(input_name)
    if sock is None:
        return False
    try:
        sock.default_value = value
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def clear_scene():
    # Ensure object mode
    if bpy.ops.object.mode_set.poll():
        try:
            bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='OBJECT')
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Delete all objects
    deselect_all()
    for obj in list(bpy.data.objects):
        obj.select_set(True)
    if bpy.ops.object.delete.poll():

def make_material_oil():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Oil")
    # NOTE: Do not set mat.use_nodes (deprecated). Node trees exist by default.
    mat.use_nodes = True

    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links

    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
    out.location = (620, 0)

    principled = nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled")
    principled.location = (220, 0)

    # Amber-gold oil (surface)
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Base Color", (0.85, 0.65, 0.15, 1.0))
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Transmission Weight", 1.0)
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "IOR", 1.47)
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Roughness", 0.035)

    # Subsurface (socket names differ across versions); keep it optional.
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Subsurface Weight", 0.03)
    # Avoid hardcoding "Subsurface Color" (missing in some 5.0 builds).

    # Volume absorption for rich color depth
    vol_abs = nodes.new("ShaderNodeVolumeAbsorption")
    vol_abs.location = (220, -240)
    safe_set_node_input(vol_abs, "Color", (0.95, 0.70, 0.20, 1.0))
    safe_set_node_input(vol_abs, "Density", 2.5)

    # Subtle micro-variation in roughness
    noise = nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
    noise.location = (-240, -40)
    safe_set_node_input(noise, "Scale", 25.0)
    safe_set_node_input(noise, "Detail", 2.0)
    safe_set_node_input(noise, "Roughness", 0.5)

    mapr = nodes.new("ShaderNodeMapRange")
    mapr.location = (0, -40)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "From Min", 0.3)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "From Max", 0.7)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "To Min", 0.02)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "To Max", 0.06)

    links.new(noise.outputs.get("Fac"), mapr.inputs.get("Value"))
    links.new(mapr.outputs.get("Result"), principled.inputs.get("Roughness"))

    links.new(principled.outputs.get("BSDF"), out.inputs.get("Surface"))
    links.new(vol_abs.outputs.get("Volume"), out.inputs.get("Volume"))

    return mat


def make_material_glass():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Glass")

    nt = mat.node_tree

def create_table_and_backdrop(table_mat):
    # Table plane
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=2.0, location=(0, 0, 0))
    table = bpy.context.active_object
    table.name = "Table"
    table.data.materials.append(table_mat)

    # Backdrop plane
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=2.0, location=(0, 0.7, 1.0))
    back = bpy.context.active_object
    back.name = "Backdrop"
    back.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0, 0)
    back.data.materials.append(table_mat)

    set_active(back)
    if bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth.poll():
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    return table, back


def create_glass(glass_mat):
    radius = 0.04
    height = 0.12

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=128, radius=radius, depth=height, location=(0, 0, height * 0.5))
    glass = bpy.context.active_object
    glass.name = "Glass"

    # Remove top face to make it open
    me = glass.data
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)

    top_z = max(v.co.z for v in bm.verts)
    faces_top = [f for f in bm.faces if all(v.co.z > top_z - 1e-6 for v in f.verts)]
    if faces_top:
        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=faces_top, context='FACES')

    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()

    solid = glass.modifiers.new(name="Solidify", type='SOLIDIFY')
    solid.thickness = -0.003
    solid.offset = 1.0

    bev = glass.modifiers.new(name="Bevel", type='BEVEL')
    bev.width = 0.001
    bev.segments = 3

    set_active(glass)
    if bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth.poll():
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    glass.data.materials.append(glass_mat)
    return glass


def create_domain_cube():
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=(0, 0, 0.25))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "FluidDomain"

    # 0.30 x 0.30 x 0.50 meters
    domain.scale = (0.15, 0.15, 0.25)

    domain.display_type = 'WIRE'
    return domain


def create_flow_inflow_emitter_volume():
    """Use a thin cylinder (volume) instead of a plane emitter.

    This avoids reliance on fset.use_plane_init (not in verified spec).
    """
    glass_rim = 0.12
    pour_height = 0.15
    z = glass_rim + pour_height

    # Stream diameter ~8mm => radius 4mm
    radius = 0.004
    depth = 0.02  # short section of fluid volume

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=64, radius=radius, depth=depth, location=(0, 0, z))
    emitter = bpy.context.active_object
    emitter.name = "OilInflow"

    emitter.hide_render = True
    emitter.display_type = 'WIRE'
    return emitter


def create_flow_initial_pool():
    radius_inner = 0.037
    height = 0.035

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=96, radius=radius_inner, depth=height, location=(0, 0, height * 0.5 + 0.002))
    pool = bpy.context.active_object
    pool.name = "OilInitialPool"
    pool.hide_render = True
    pool.display_type = 'WIRE'
    return pool

def create_lighting():
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(0.0, 0.35, 0.25))

def create_camera(glass_obj):
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0.0, -0.42, 0.12))

def setup_domain(domain_obj, oil_mat):
    mod = domain_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'DOMAIN'
    dset = mod.domain_settings  # MUST be named 'dset'

    # VERIFIED dset.* ONLY
    dset.domain_type = 'LIQUID'
    dset.resolution_max = 96
    dset.use_adaptive_timesteps = True
    dset.timesteps_max = 12

    dset.use_noise = False
    dset.noise_strength = 0.2
    dset.noise_scale = 2

    dset.vorticity = 0.05

    dset.cache_type = 'ALL'
    dset.cache_directory = CACHE_DIR

    dset.openvdb_cache_compress_type = 'ZIP'

    dset.use_flip_particles = True
    dset.flip_ratio = 1.0
    dset.particle_radius = 1.0

    dset.use_mesh = True
    dset.mesh_smoothen_pos = 2
    dset.mesh_smoothen_neg = 2
    dset.mesh_concave_upper = 1.0

    # Secondary particles: keep bubbles on, foam/spray off.
    # WARNING: in Blender, disabling particle types can delete particle systems;
    # here we only set them once on a new scene.
    dset.use_bubble_particles = True
    dset.use_foam_particles = False
    dset.use_spray_particles = False

    # Assign oil material to domain (mesh output will use it)
    if domain_obj.data.materials:
        domain_obj.data.materials[0] = oil_mat
    else:
        domain_obj.data.materials.append(oil_mat)

    return mod


def setup_flow_inflow(flow_obj):
    mod = flow_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # MUST be named 'fset'

    # VERIFIED fset.* ONLY
    fset.flow_type = 'LIQUID'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'INFLOW'

    fset.use_initial_velocity = True
    # Emit downward: negative normal velocity along emitter normals.
    fset.velocity_normal = -3.0

    fset.temperature = 0.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    return mod


def setup_flow_geometry(flow_obj):
    mod = flow_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # MUST be named 'fset'

    # VERIFIED fset.* ONLY
    fset.flow_type = 'LIQUID'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'GEOMETRY'

    fset.use_initial_velocity = False
    fset.velocity_normal = 0.0

    fset.temperature = 0.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    return mod


def setup_effector(glass_obj, table_obj):
    # Effector modifiers (no effector properties set; defaults are used)
    mod = glass_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')

    mod2 = table_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')

def bake_simulation(domain_obj):
    print("\n--- Baking Mantaflow ---")
    print(f"Cache directory: {CACHE_DIR}")

    # Domain must be active & selected for bake operators.
    set_active(domain_obj)
    depsgraph_update()

    # Try full bake first.
    try:
        if bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all.poll():
            bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all()
            print("bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all finished")
            return
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"bake_all failed: {e}")

    # Fallback: modular bakes
    for op_name, op in (
        ("bake_data", bpy.ops.fluid.bake_data),
        ("bake_mesh", bpy.ops.fluid.bake_mesh),
        ("bake_particles", bpy.ops.fluid.bake_particles),
    ):
        try:
            set_active(domain_obj)
            depsgraph_update()
            if op.poll():
                op()
                print(f"bpy.ops.fluid.{op_name} finished")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"bpy.ops.fluid.{op_name} failed: {e}")


def render_frames():
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    print("\n--- Rendering frames ---")
    for fr in range(scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end + 1):
        scene.frame_set(fr)
        depsgraph_update()
        filepath = os.path.join(FRAME_DIR, f"{ASSET_NAME}_{fr:04d}.png")
        scene.render.filepath = filepath
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
        print(f"Rendered frame {fr} -> {filepath}")


def save_blend():
    blend_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f"{ASSET_NAME}.blend")
    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=blend_path)
    print(f"Saved .blend to: {blend_path}")


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    clear_scene()
    setup_scene()

    oil_mat = make_material_oil()
    glass_mat = make_material_glass()
    table_mat = make_material_table()

    table, back = create_table_and_backdrop(table_mat)
    glass = create_glass(glass_mat)

    # Fluid objects
    domain = create_domain_cube()
    inflow = create_flow_inflow_emitter_volume()
    pool = create_flow_initial_pool()

    # Camera and lights
    create_lighting()
    create_camera(glass)

    # Fluid modifiers (STRICT usage)
    setup_domain(domain, oil_mat)
    setup_flow_inflow(inflow)
    setup_flow_geometry(pool)
    setup_effector(glass, table)

    depsgraph_update()

    # Inform about spec limitations
    print("\n--- Spec limitations ---")
    print("Requested but not in VERIFIED API spec, so not set:")
    print("- Flow use_plane_init (workaround: inflow uses a volume cylinder emitter)")
    print("- Viscosity (viscosity_base / viscosity_exponent)")
    print("- Adaptive domain bounds setting")
    print("- Explicit surface tension / mesh_smoothness controls")

    # Bake
    bake_simulation(domain)

    # Render
    render_frames()

    # Save .blend
    save_blend()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

{"code":"import bpy
import os
import sys
import math
import shutil
from mathutils import Vector
import bmesh

# =============================================================
# Oil Pour (Mantaflow Liquid) - Blender 5.0
# Iteration 2 (specfix): output-dir driven cache + cache-size verification
#
# IMPORTANT:
# - dset.* and fset.* assignments use ONLY VERIFIED attributes provided.
# - This script builds a full scene, bakes Mantaflow cache, renders frames,
#   and saves a .blend for inspection.
# =============================================================

ASSET_NAME = "oil_pour_20260202_021508"
FRAME_START = 1
FRAME_END = 48
FPS = 24

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Output dir handling (wrapper provides --output_dir)
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_output_dir_from_argv(default_dir: str) -> str:
    """Parse --output_dir <path> from Blender sys.argv.

    Blender convention: args after '--' are user script args.
    Wrapper calls blender ... --python script.py -- --output_dir /path
    """
    argv = sys.argv
    if "--" in argv:
        argv = argv[argv.index("--") + 1:]
    else:
        argv = []

    out_dir = None
    for i, a in enumerate(argv):
        if a == "--output_dir" and i + 1 < len(argv):
            out_dir = argv[i + 1]
            break
    return out_dir if out_dir else default_dir


DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR = os.path.join("/tmp", "blender_vfx", ASSET_NAME)
OUTPUT_DIR = parse_output_dir_from_argv(DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR)
FRAME_DIR = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "frames")
# IMPORTANT: cache must live inside OUTPUT_DIR so the artifact gate can see it.
CACHE_DIR = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "cache", "FluidDomain")

for p in (OUTPUT_DIR, FRAME_DIR, CACHE_DIR):
    os.makedirs(p, exist_ok=True)


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Utilities
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def deselect_all():
    for o in bpy.context.view_layer.objects:
        o.select_set(False)


def set_active(obj):
    deselect_all()
    obj.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = obj


def depsgraph_update():
    """Try to update depsgraph safely."""
    try:
        bpy.context.view_layer.depsgraph.update()
    except Exception:
        try:
            bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        except Exception:
            pass


def look_at(obj, target, track='-Z', up='Y'):
    direction = (target - obj.location).normalized()
    quat = direction.to_track_quat(track, up)
    obj.rotation_euler = quat.to_euler()


def safe_set_node_input(node, input_name, value):
    """Set node input by name if it exists (avoid KeyError across versions)."""
    sock = node.inputs.get(input_name)
    if sock is None:
        return False
    try:
        sock.default_value = value
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def dir_size_bytes(path: str) -> int:
    total = 0
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return 0
    for root, _dirs, files in os.walk(path):
        for f in files:
            fp = os.path.join(root, f)
            try:
                total += os.path.getsize(fp)
            except OSError:
                pass
    return total


def clear_scene():
    # Ensure object mode
    if bpy.ops.object.mode_set.poll():
        try:
            bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode='OBJECT')
        except Exception:
            pass

    # Delete all objects
    deselect_all()
    for obj in list(bpy.data.objects):
        obj.select_set(True)
    if bpy.ops.object.delete.poll():
        bpy.ops.object.delete(use_global=False)

    # Remove orphan data blocks (conservative)
    for datablock in (bpy.data.meshes, bpy.data.materials, bpy.data.lights, bpy.data.cameras):
        for block in list(datablock):
            if block.users == 0:
                datablock.remove(block)


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Scene setup
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def setup_scene():
    scene = bpy.context.scene

    scene.frame_start = FRAME_START
    scene.frame_end = FRAME_END
    scene.render.fps = FPS

    scene.render.engine = 'CYCLES'
    scene.cycles.samples = 256
    scene.cycles.device = 'GPU'

    scene.render.resolution_x = 1920
    scene.render.resolution_y = 1080
    scene.render.resolution_percentage = 100

    scene.render.image_settings.file_format = 'PNG'
    scene.render.image_settings.color_mode = 'RGBA'
    scene.render.film_transparent = False

    # Warm product look
    try:
        scene.view_settings.view_transform = 'Filmic'
        scene.view_settings.look = 'Medium High Contrast'
        scene.view_settings.exposure = 0.2
    except Exception:
        pass


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Materials
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def make_material_oil():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Oil")
    # Do NOT set Material.use_nodes (deprecated). Nodes exist by default.
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
    out.location = (620, 0)

    principled = nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled")
    principled.location = (220, 0)

    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Base Color", (0.85, 0.65, 0.15, 1.0))
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Transmission Weight", 1.0)
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "IOR", 1.47)
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Roughness", 0.035)

    # Subsurface is optional; socket names vary.
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Subsurface Weight", 0.03)

    # Volume absorption
    vol_abs = nodes.new("ShaderNodeVolumeAbsorption")
    vol_abs.location = (220, -240)
    safe_set_node_input(vol_abs, "Color", (0.95, 0.70, 0.20, 1.0))
    safe_set_node_input(vol_abs, "Density", 2.5)

    # Roughness micro-variation
    noise = nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
    noise.location = (-240, -40)
    safe_set_node_input(noise, "Scale", 25.0)
    safe_set_node_input(noise, "Detail", 2.0)
    safe_set_node_input(noise, "Roughness", 0.5)

    mapr = nodes.new("ShaderNodeMapRange")
    mapr.location = (0, -40)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "From Min", 0.3)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "From Max", 0.7)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "To Min", 0.02)
    safe_set_node_input(mapr, "To Max", 0.06)

    # Use get() to avoid exceptions if sockets rename
    if noise.outputs.get("Fac") and mapr.inputs.get("Value"):
        links.new(noise.outputs.get("Fac"), mapr.inputs.get("Value"))
    if mapr.outputs.get("Result") and principled.inputs.get("Roughness"):
        links.new(mapr.outputs.get("Result"), principled.inputs.get("Roughness"))

    links.new(principled.outputs.get("BSDF"), out.inputs.get("Surface"))
    links.new(vol_abs.outputs.get("Volume"), out.inputs.get("Volume"))

    return mat


def make_material_glass():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Glass")
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes
    links = nt.links
    nodes.clear()

    out = nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputMaterial")
    out.location = (460, 0)

    principled = nodes.new("ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled")
    principled.location = (140, 0)

    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Base Color", (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0))
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Transmission Weight", 1.0)
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "IOR", 1.52)
    safe_set_node_input(principled, "Roughness", 0.0)

    links.new(principled.outputs.get("BSDF"), out.inputs.get("Surface"))
    return mat


def make_material_table():
    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(name="MAT_Table")
    nt = mat.node_tree
    nodes = nt.nodes

    # Default nodes exist; keep and just tweak
    principled = nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
    if principled:
        safe_set_node_input(principled, "Base Color", (0.95, 0.93, 0.90, 1.0))
        safe_set_node_input(principled, "Roughness", 0.45)

    return mat


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Geometry creation
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def create_table_and_backdrop(table_mat):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=2.0, location=(0, 0, 0))
    table = bpy.context.active_object
    table.name = "Table"
    table.data.materials.append(table_mat)

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_plane_add(size=2.0, location=(0, 0.7, 1.0))
    back = bpy.context.active_object
    back.name = "Backdrop"
    back.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0, 0)
    back.data.materials.append(table_mat)

    set_active(back)
    if bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth.poll():
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    return table, back


def create_glass(glass_mat):
    radius = 0.04
    height = 0.12

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=128, radius=radius, depth=height, location=(0, 0, height * 0.5))
    glass = bpy.context.active_object
    glass.name = "Glass"

    # Remove top face to make it open
    me = glass.data
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)

    top_z = max(v.co.z for v in bm.verts)
    faces_top = [f for f in bm.faces if all(v.co.z > top_z - 1e-6 for v in f.verts)]
    if faces_top:
        bmesh.ops.delete(bm, geom=faces_top, context='FACES')

    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()

    # Wall thickness + rim highlight
    solid = glass.modifiers.new(name="Solidify", type='SOLIDIFY')
    solid.thickness = -0.003
    solid.offset = 1.0

    bev = glass.modifiers.new(name="Bevel", type='BEVEL')
    bev.width = 0.001
    bev.segments = 3

    set_active(glass)
    if bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth.poll():
        bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

    glass.data.materials.append(glass_mat)
    return glass


def create_domain_cube():
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=1.0, location=(0, 0, 0.25))
    domain = bpy.context.active_object
    domain.name = "FluidDomain"
    domain.scale = (0.15, 0.15, 0.25)
    domain.display_type = 'WIRE'
    return domain


def create_flow_inflow_emitter_volume():
    """Thin cylinder inflow (volume) to avoid needing plane-init settings."""
    glass_rim = 0.12
    pour_height = 0.15
    z = glass_rim + pour_height

    radius = 0.004
    depth = 0.02
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=64, radius=radius, depth=depth, location=(0, 0, z))
    emitter = bpy.context.active_object
    emitter.name = "OilInflow"
    emitter.hide_render = True
    emitter.display_type = 'WIRE'
    return emitter


def create_flow_initial_pool():
    radius_inner = 0.037
    height = 0.035

    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cylinder_add(vertices=96, radius=radius_inner, depth=height, location=(0, 0, height * 0.5 + 0.002))
    pool = bpy.context.active_object
    pool.name = "OilInitialPool"
    pool.hide_render = True
    pool.display_type = 'WIRE'
    return pool


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Lighting and Camera
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def create_lighting():
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(0.0, 0.35, 0.25))
    key = bpy.context.active_object
    key.name = "Light_Key_Back"
    key.data.energy = 1200
    key.data.size = 0.35
    key.data.color = (1.0, 0.86, 0.55)
    look_at(key, Vector((0, 0, 0.08)), track='-Z', up='Y')

    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(-0.22, -0.25, 0.18))
    fill = bpy.context.active_object
    fill.name = "Light_Fill"
    fill.data.energy = 350
    fill.data.size = 0.45
    fill.data.color = (1.0, 0.95, 0.85)
    look_at(fill, Vector((0, 0, 0.08)), track='-Z', up='Y')

    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type='AREA', location=(0.25, -0.10, 0.20))
    rim = bpy.context.active_object
    rim.name = "Light_Rim"
    rim.data.energy = 220
    rim.data.size = 0.25
    rim.data.color = (1.0, 0.90, 0.75)
    look_at(rim, Vector((0, 0, 0.08)), track='-Z', up='Y')


def create_camera(glass_obj):
    bpy.ops.object.camera_add(location=(0.0, -0.42, 0.12))
    cam = bpy.context.active_object
    cam.name = "Camera"
    cam.data.lens = 85

    try:
        cam.data.dof.use_dof = True
        cam.data.dof.focus_object = glass_obj
        cam.data.dof.aperture_fstop = 2.4
    except Exception:
        pass

    look_at(cam, Vector((0, 0, 0.085)), track='-Z', up='Y')
    bpy.context.scene.camera = cam
    return cam


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Fluid setup (STRICT: only verified dset.* and fset.* attributes)
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def setup_domain(domain_obj, oil_mat):
    mod = domain_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'DOMAIN'
    dset = mod.domain_settings  # MUST be named 'dset'

    # VERIFIED dset.* ONLY
    dset.domain_type = 'LIQUID'
    dset.resolution_max = 96
    dset.use_adaptive_timesteps = True
    dset.timesteps_max = 12

    dset.use_noise = False
    dset.noise_strength = 0.2
    dset.noise_scale = 2

    dset.vorticity = 0.05

    dset.cache_type = 'ALL'
    dset.cache_directory = CACHE_DIR

    dset.openvdb_cache_compress_type = 'ZIP'

    dset.use_flip_particles = True
    dset.flip_ratio = 1.0
    dset.particle_radius = 1.0

    dset.use_mesh = True
    dset.mesh_smoothen_pos = 2
    dset.mesh_smoothen_neg = 2
    dset.mesh_concave_upper = 1.0

    # Secondary particles
    dset.use_bubble_particles = True
    dset.use_foam_particles = False
    dset.use_spray_particles = False

    # Assign oil material to domain mesh output
    if domain_obj.data.materials:
        domain_obj.data.materials[0] = oil_mat
    else:
        domain_obj.data.materials.append(oil_mat)

    return mod


def setup_flow_inflow(flow_obj):
    mod = flow_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # MUST be named 'fset'

    # VERIFIED fset.* ONLY
    fset.flow_type = 'LIQUID'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'INFLOW'

    fset.use_initial_velocity = True
    fset.velocity_normal = -3.0

    fset.temperature = 0.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    return mod


def setup_flow_geometry(flow_obj):
    mod = flow_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'FLOW'
    fset = mod.flow_settings  # MUST be named 'fset'

    # VERIFIED fset.* ONLY
    fset.flow_type = 'LIQUID'
    fset.flow_behavior = 'GEOMETRY'

    fset.use_initial_velocity = False
    fset.velocity_normal = 0.0

    fset.temperature = 0.0
    fset.density = 1.0

    return mod


def setup_effector(glass_obj, table_obj):
    mod = glass_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod.fluid_type = 'EFFECTOR'

    mod2 = table_obj.modifiers.new(name='Fluid', type='FLUID')
    mod2.fluid_type = 'EFFECTOR'


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Baking and Rendering
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def bake_ops_modular(domain_obj):
    """Run modular bake ops (data -> mesh -> particles)."""
    set_active(domain_obj)
    depsgraph_update()

    # Data
    if bpy.ops.fluid.bake_data.poll():
        bpy.ops.fluid.bake_data()

    set_active(domain_obj)
    depsgraph_update()

    # Mesh
    if bpy.ops.fluid.bake_mesh.poll():
        bpy.ops.fluid.bake_mesh()

    set_active(domain_obj)
    depsgraph_update()

    # Particles
    if bpy.ops.fluid.bake_particles.poll():
        bpy.ops.fluid.bake_particles()


def bake_simulation(domain_obj, domain_mod):
    """Bake Mantaflow cache to CACHE_DIR and verify cache size."""
    print("\n--- Output paths ---")
    print(f"OUTPUT_DIR: {OUTPUT_DIR}")
    print(f"FRAME_DIR:  {FRAME_DIR}")
    print(f"CACHE_DIR:  {CACHE_DIR}")

    # Safety: ensure cache dir exists
    os.makedirs(CACHE_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    print("\n--- Baking Mantaflow ---")
    print("Baking operators require the domain to be active + selected")

    # Ensure domain is active
    set_active(domain_obj)
    depsgraph_update()

    # Try bake_all (if available), then ALWAYS run modular bakes as requested.
    try:
        if bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all.poll():
            bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all()
            print("bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all finished")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"bpy.ops.fluid.bake_all failed: {e}")

    # Always run modular sequence to force outputs
    try:
        bake_ops_modular(domain_obj)
        print("Modular bake sequence finished")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Modular bake sequence failed: {e}")

    depsgraph_update()

    # Post-bake verification
    size1 = dir_size_bytes(CACHE_DIR)
    print(f"Cache dir size after bake: {size1 / (1024 * 1024):.2f} MB")

    # If Blender internally wrote to a different folder (shouldn't, since we set dset.cache_directory),
    # copy it into CACHE_DIR as a last resort.
    try:
        dset = domain_mod.domain_settings
        src_cache = dset.cache_directory
        if src_cache and os.path.abspath(src_cache) != os.path.abspath(CACHE_DIR):
            print(f"Cache directory mismatch. Copying from {src_cache} -> {CACHE_DIR}")
            if os.path.exists(src_cache):
                shutil.copytree(src_cache, CACHE_DIR, dirs_exist_ok=True)
    except Exception:
        pass

    size2 = dir_size_bytes(CACHE_DIR)
    if size2 < 1 * 1024 * 1024:
        print("\n[ERROR] Cache too small (< 1MB). Retrying modular bake once...")
        try:
            bake_ops_modular(domain_obj)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Retry modular bake failed: {e}")

    size3 = dir_size_bytes(CACHE_DIR)
    print(f"Cache dir size final: {size3 / (1024 * 1024):.2f} MB")


def render_frames():
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    print("\n--- Rendering frames ---")

    for fr in range(scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end + 1):
        scene.frame_set(fr)
        depsgraph_update()

        filepath = os.path.join(FRAME_DIR, f"{ASSET_NAME}_{fr:04d}.png")
        scene.render.filepath = filepath
        bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)

        # Verbose but useful in headless runs
        if fr in (scene.frame_start, (scene.frame_start + scene.frame_end) // 2, scene.frame_end):
            print(f"Rendered frame {fr} -> {filepath}")


def save_blend():
    blend_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f"{ASSET_NAME}.blend")
    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=blend_path)
    print(f"Saved .blend to: {blend_path}")


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# -------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    clear_scene()
    setup_scene()

    oil_mat = make_material_oil()
    glass_mat = make_material_glass()
    table_mat = make_material_table()

    table, back = create_table_and_backdrop(table_mat)
    glass = create_glass(glass_mat)

    # Fluid objects
    domain = create_domain_cube()
    inflow = create_flow_inflow_emitter_volume()
    pool = create_flow_initial_pool()

    # Camera and lights
    create_lighting()
    create_camera(glass)

    # Fluid modifiers
    domain_mod = setup_domain(domain, oil_mat)
    setup_flow_inflow(inflow)
    setup_flow_geometry(pool)
    setup_effector(glass, table)

    depsgraph_update()

    print("\n--- Spec limitations ---")
    print("Requested but not in VERIFIED API spec, so not set:")
    print("- Flow use_plane_init (workaround: volume cylinder inflow emitter)")
    print("- Viscosity (viscosity_base / viscosity_exponent)")
    print("- Adaptive domain bounds setting")
    print("- Explicit surface tension / mesh_smoothness controls")

    # Bake and verify
    bake_simulation(domain, domain_mod)

    # Render
    render_frames()

    # Save
    save_blend()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
